  "text": "Mara kept her hand raised until the harbor master lowered his lantern.

“Did you see her?” she asked.

He looked at the empty streetlamp. “See who?”

The woman had already turned toward the steps. Mara followed her gaze. Water was rising between the stones, though the square lay well above the quay. It carried a scrap of paper to Mara’s boot. She bent and picked it up.

It was the photograph, soft with rain. The little girl stood beside the harbor gate, one hand lifted. Where Mara remembered a woman at her side, there was only a pale blur.

The harbor master took a step toward the bell tower. “We have to close the gate.”

“It’s closed,” the woman said.

Another metallic knock came from below. Then three quick footsteps sounded on the steps, exactly as Mara had heard them in the shell. She looked down. No one was there.

The woman touched the photograph. “I waited for you that night,” she said. “I heard you coming, but you never reached the top.”

Mara turned the shell over. A thin thread of red wool caught on its chipped edge. She remembered a coat with red mittens tied through the sleeves, and one mitten dragging behind her as she ran. She remembered stopping halfway up the steps because someone had called from the water.

The bell began to ring. Mara set the shell on the highest step. For a moment, a small wet hand appeared beside it. Mara held out the photograph, and the hand took it.

When the bell fell silent, the water between the stones was gone."
